title: Ops Journal: Microflow compiler for safe, observable one-click remediations
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Goal: Build a lightweight microflow compiler ("ops-journal") that converts curated runbook fragments into single-button, auditable remediation actions with built-in telemetry and safety gates. The output should be idempotent, reversible where possible, and include automatic pre-checks and post-checks. Scope: compiler, runtime adapter (execution shim), audit/event envelope, basic UI hook for the Console, and a canary rollout plan for firstline usage. Non-goals: full RBAC integration (will be staged), complex policy language (we'll start with typed inputs + assertions).

Background: Pager incident on 2026-02-14 showed the majority of toil came from repetitive multi-step fixes that junior responders executed. We want to streamline common recovery paths without removing human oversight. The microflow compiler will let SRE/Support authors assemble fragments from the snippet registry and produce a single safe action with synthesized pre/post checks.

Design decisions and trade-offs so far:
- "Typed inputs + assertions" instead of a full DSL to keep surface area small and audit-friendly. (Decision: Asha + Evelyn, 2026-03-03)
- Execution model: synchronous with enforced timeouts and an async fallback path for long-running ops. This preserves immediate feedback for short remediations.
- Telemetry: emit structured events for start/step/result to ops-journal Grafana panel. Minimal token-level logging in the Console traces to help cost attribution.
- Safety: each microflow must declare an impact level (none/low/medium/high). High-impact flows require a secondary approver and cannot be executed from the user-facing Console until approved.

Milestones completed:
- Spec doc (Confluence): https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/OPS/Ops+Journal+Microflow+Compiler+Spec (initial draft)
- Snippet registry classifier prototype: repo branch at https://github.com/redwood-inference/ops-tooling/tree/feature/snippet-classifier
- Basic runtime shim PoC: https://github.com/redwood-inference/ops-tooling/pull/482 (experimental)

Next steps / open tasks:
1) Finish compiler core (validation, input typing, assertion engine) -- in progress, target PR end of week.
2) Add audit envelope + event schema and wire to Grafana dashboard (ops-journal panel).
3) UX hook: Console button + modal for preflight checks (design review scheduled with UX, 2026-03-11).
4) Create canary group in Dedicated/Hosted for pilot (SRE + Support).
5) Security review for approval workflow and execution IAM privileges (blocked until security sign-off).

Acceptance criteria:
- Compiler converts at least 5 curated snippets into a single microflow with typed inputs and assertions.
- Execution emits structured telemetry events for each microflow step visible in Grafana.
- Safety gating is enforced: high-impact flows blocked without approver.
- Two pilot incidents successfully remediated via the microflow by the pilot group with postmortem notes.

Links / artifacts:
- Spec (Confluence): https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/OPS/Ops+Journal+Microflow+Compiler+Spec
- PR (PoC): https://github.com/redwood-inference/ops-tooling/pull/482
- Grafana panel (ops-journal): https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/ops/ops-journal-events
- Design mockups (Drive): https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1f-pilot-ui-mockups

Risks / mitigation:
- Risk: Accidentally exposing high-privilege operations via a one-click button. Mitigation: conservative default to "manual" for any snippet tagged with privileged labels; security review required before enabling in Console.
- Risk: Telemetry volume spike. Mitigation: sample high-frequency flows and include a per-flow telemetry budget that the compiler enforces.
